technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The objective form of the social labour expended in producing a commodity, measured by the labour it contains.
The useful quality of a commodity, which is incommensurable with exchange-value.
The social form of value whose augmentation drives the personified capitalist.
The worker's capacity to work, which is what the worker actually sells to the capitalist.

technical_terms.term: value of labour / price of labour
technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The wage read as the value or price of labour, which Marx calls an irrational expression for labour-power.
The regulating price of labour, which classical economy took to be its value in money.
The value a capitalist gets from labour beyond the value of the labour-power, shown here as the surplus product.
The part of the working day beyond necessary labour, which the wage form hides.
The part of the working day that replaces the value of labour-power.
The division the wage form conceals, since all labour appears as paid.
The factor that sets the rate of surplus-value.
The part of capital that is advanced as wages and returns as the labourer's reproduced fund.
The means of production whose value passes into the product unchanged.
All capital, in the end, is surplus-value that has been reconverted into capital.
Employing surplus-value as capital, reconverting it into capital.
Repeated production on the old scale, where all surplus-value is consumed.

technical_terms.term: reproduction on a progressively increasing scale
technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Accumulation seen concretely: the circle becomes a spiral.
variants_seen: reproduction on a progressively increasing scale

technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The labourer's consumption that reproduces labour-power is productive for capital; the rest is unproductive.
Labour that produces surplus-value for capital, as against what Smith's analysis wrongly assumes.
The market phase where capital is bought and sold, distinct from production.
Production for sale, whose laws of property turn into the laws of capitalist appropriation.
The free sale of labour-power as a commodity, which makes commodity production general.
The two converted forms of the wage: pay by time or by product, both derived from the value of labour-power.
Money wages versus the means of subsistence they buy.
The supposed fixed fund of subsistence for wages, which Marx calls a dogma.
The working time that counts for value, measured by the experimentally fixed product.
The national norm of labour intensity, which sets the unit of universal labour.
Labour's rising productivity, which increases the mass of products and of surplus-value.
The capitalist's own term for machinery; Marx says the distinction is only a formal difference of circulation.

technical_terms.term: means of production / means of subsistence
technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The material forms of capital: tools and materials, and the goods that feed labourers.
The new value a working day creates, used to show piece-wage's relation to time-wage.
The price of one hour of labour, the unit by which time-wages are measured.
Surplus-value as the periodic fruit of capital, which the capitalist can spend.
The two shares into which surplus-value is split: spending and reinvesting.

voice_attribution_risks.note: Long run of classical economists' views in Marx's voice; the 'value of labour' is a view he is criticising.
Say's 'What is value?' answer is quoted inside Marx's Proudhon footnote; easy to read as Marx's.
Competition argument includes the capitalist's own complaint; the bakers' spokesman speaks as a capitalist, so a reader may take it as Marx's.
The capitalist's view is stated 'rightly' in Marx's voice; irony, not endorsement.
Carey's views are set out at length before Marx's rebuttal in the same paragraph.
Unnamed out-of-work man and the Potter letter's reasoning are quoted; reader must not take 'the public' as Marx's view.
Potter's 'machinery' is a euphemism for living workers; the Times reply reverses it.
A Ricardian manufacturer's rebuke of Malthus; Marx reports it, then shows its limits.
Malthus's line that glut means large profits; Marx quotes but does not endorse.
J. S. Mill quoted for 'wages have no productive power'; Marx answers at once.
Fawcett's 'wage-fund' sentence is stated before Marx's exposure of the dodge.

irony_examples.note: Say defines value as 'what a thing is worth'; Marx mocks the circularity.
The Morning Star's 'moral indignation' over slavery, while ignoring wage labour.
The 'jeremiad' of the full-priced baker is ironic; the capitalist's own complaint shows he misunderstands unpaid labour.
'Rightly knocks on the head' reads as a sarcastic endorsement of the capitalist's rebuttal.
'The best of it' and 'Bastiat' are ironic jibes at Carey.
The Times mocks Potter's 'human machinery' and its 'moral workhouse' proposal.
The Durham 'bondage' description and the dung-as-perquisite joke expose capital's claim on labour.
'What would the good Dr. Aikin say...' is a sarcastic aside on Manchester's wealth.
Senior's 'abstinence' is a 'sycophantic phrase', i.e., mock-scientific.
The capitalist as 'modern penitent of Vishnu' and the Georgian slave-owner image are mock-pious.
Count Rumford 'to the great satisfaction of God and man' is a sneer.
The Speenhamland 'English Dogberries' are a comic image of officious squires.
The Essay on Trade's wish to match French and Dutch wages is called 'the innermost secret soul' of English capital.
'An uncommonly knowing dodge' mocks the wage-fund logic.

hard_passages.why: Very long argument about value, price, cost of production and classical method; many clauses.
Dense counterfactual on exchange of labour for labour; footnote quotes add layers.
A formula and a sentence about the price of an hour split across paragraphs.
Long chain of competitive effects, with nested quotes and several footnotes.
Long footnote on 'stinting' and 'sweating' in engineering trades, with Morton's ironic quote.
Piece-wage arithmetic plus Ure's cancelling phrase in a footnote.
Two-level argument: money as a token of labour, the labour-fund and the 'order-notes' metaphor.
Dense sentence chain on alienation, reproduction and the sine qua non.
Very long single paragraph on the reversal of the laws of property into appropriation.
Long argument about commodity production turning into capitalist appropriation.
Long sentence about personified capital and the drive to expand value.
Dense productivity and value argument with several embedded clauses.
Long argument on depreciation, science and chemistry as sources of capital's power of expansion.
Long footnote on Say and Ricardo's productivity dispute, in French and English.
Dogma of the labour fund set against Bentham and Mill; many footnotes.
